key_insight: A transversely isotropic model with a deformation-dependent semisoft modulus captures stiffness anisotropy and allows finite reorientation onset followed by a broad, flatter stress plateau.
engineering_relevance: The model supports mechanical analysis of main-chain liquid crystal elastomers whose stiffness and deformation response depend strongly on loading direction.
method: Combine finite-strain, isothermal network elasticity with a deformation-dependent quadratic semisoft penalty.
Use a weak-fluctuation statistical closure to obtain an exponential transition from initial to residual semisoft modulus.
Derive perpendicular-tension relations and couple director rotation, shear and lateral contraction under oblique tension.
evidence_signal: Comparisons with orientation-dependent measurements using one common parameter set capture the principal stiffness contrast and broad perpendicular plateau.
watch_item: Discrepancies remain in oblique stresses and intermediate-angle initial moduli, limiting confidence for off-axis predictions.
paper_title: A transversely isotropic constitutive model for semisoft elasticity in main-chain liquid crystal elastomers
